back:
Compiler extensions are compiler-specific extra behaviors that are not part of standard C++. They are often enabled by default.

Code that uses them may not compile (or may not run correctly) on other compilers. They are never necessary. Disable them so you learn standard C++ and stay portable.

Typical flags: MSVC /permissive- (Conformance mode), GCC/Clang -pedantic-errors.
front: What are compiler extensions, and why should you disable them?
